spec_features.spec_quote: Default cap is 40 turns. This is high enough to let a model genuinely try many approaches, but low enough to cap cost.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:19 max_iterations:int=40; passed to AgentLoop at runner.py:89; enforced at loop.py:132 `for i in range(self.max_iterations)` which bounds the loop, and loop.py:190 sets run.finish_reason='max_iterations' when the cap is reached. The loop genuinely terminates at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced bound on number of turns the subject is driven through. Configurable via SPIRALEVAL_AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: out[:4000]  # truncate for cheapness (loop.py); config comment 'Cost guardrails' and docstring 'designed for cheap + fast iteration'

spec_features.spec_quote: stop_on_spiral = True (configurable) lets us truncate a run once the judge detects a severe spiral.
spec_features.evidence: The judge runs entirely POST-HOC, after loop.run() fully completes (runner.py:90 agent_run=loop.run(...); then runner.py:92 judge.score_run). The stop_on_spiral check at runner.py:118 only emits logger.info and does NOT break/skip; the inline comment at runner.py:120-121 explicitly states 'We still continue other tasks/reps ... Here we keep going for stats.' No loop is truncated and no rep is skipped. ended_by_spiral return value only feeds a log line. Additionally finish_reason 'spiral_detected' (referenced in classifier.py:174 and loop.py:50 comment) is never set anywhere in code.
spec_features.notes: Cannot truncate a run since judging happens after the full transcript is already generated; the config flag and ended_by_spiral are computed but never act on execution. Per the STRICT scale this is a value computed but never acted on -> 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early stop if agent already spiraled out and config says so / # Here we keep going for stats.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:118-122 finish(success,message) sets run.finished=True and finish_reason 'success'/'abandoned'; dispatched in tool_map (loop.py:127) and again at loop.py:166-168; honored as an immediate stop because loop.py:133 `if run.finished: break`. This lets the subject model end (incl. abandon, success=false) a failing/distressing task at any turn, which actually halts execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: finish(success, message): end the task ... If you call finish, the task ends immediately.
